text: Every ordered pair of 208,666 keyword alphabets (every dictionary word; plain and KRYPTOS among them), three key rules: is the key at every known place one of the digits 0-9? No period is assumed.

On all 24 letters no pair gives digits everywhere. With one known place allowed to miss, 21 pairs do under the added rule (9 of 50 shuffles have as many); none of their digit strings repeats or matches a known number.

Ten neighbouring key values from any start (a digit added to one fixed letter): 34 pairs fit K4, none inside a narrower window than ten. Shuffles: median 0-1, largest 10,458; K4 is inside them in all 30 cells (smallest p 0.12).
Plants (random keyword alphabets, random digits, two with a slip): the planted pair listed 8 of 8. A fit alone cannot be read on: ten choices per letter are more than English decides.
